subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename bootstrap files as a core hook contract, or keep bootstrap-extra-files limited to recognized workspace filenames?
rationale: This changes deterministic system-prompt context and the public hook file-loading contract, so maintainer intent is needed before merge.

options.title: Approve repaired hook contract
options.body: Allow configured custom-basename files through the hook after the linked PR or replacement is rebased and preserves path guards, budgets, and session filtering.

options.title: Keep recognized basenames only
options.body: Reject arbitrary workspace-file injection and close or redirect custom-file requests to narrower first-class filename or workspace-convention proposals.

options.title: Defer to broader context API
options.body: Keep this issue as design input while maintainers define a broader context/bootstrap API instead of committing to raw hook paths now.

recommendation.title: Approve repaired hook contract
recommendation.body: Allow configured custom-basename files through the hook after the linked PR or replacement is rebased and preserves path guards, budgets, and session filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: He has recent current-main ownership in the workspace bootstrap path and authored boundary-safe read refactors that constrain the safe implementation shape.
